title: Low-temperature Quantum-corrected Holographic Transport with Momentum Relaxation
authors: Suman Das, Sabyasachi Maulik, Leopoldo A. Pando Zayas, Jingchao Zhang
abstract: We determine the quantum corrections to transport arising from fluctuations of the near-AdS${}_2$ throat of near-extremal black branes in holographic models with momentum relaxation. By computing the shear viscosity and electrical conductivity at both zero and finite chemical potential, we uncover a universal low-temperature enhancement of transport generated by Schwarzian quantum fluctuations. Specifically, transport coefficients extracted from retarded Green's functions increase throughout the regime $C T \ll 1$. For operators with Schwarzian scaling dimension $Δ>1$, this enhancement is preceded by a universal minimum at a characteristic temperature $T_{\rm min} \propto C^{-1}$, leading to a non-monotonic temperature dependence strikingly similar to that observed in many correlated materials. In contrast, for the case $Δ=1$, relevant for the electrical conductivity, the transport coefficient evolves monotonically toward a constant value. Our results identify universal signatures of near-horizon quantum gravity in the transport properties of holographic quantum matter.
summary: This paper calculates how quantum fluctuations modify transport properties like viscosity and conductivity near extremal black branes using the AdS/CFT correspondence. It finds universal low-temperature enhancements, predicting non-monotonic temperature dependence similar to that observed in real correlated materials. This work provides holographic signatures of quantum gravity effects on condensed matter transport.
main_problem: The study determines quantum corrections to transport properties, such as shear viscosity and electrical conductivity, at low temperatures in holographic models that incorporate momentum relaxation.
main_result: Quantum fluctuations lead to a universal low-temperature enhancement of transport; specifically, for certain operators, this manifests as a non-monotonic temperature dependence with a minimum at $T_{m min} \propto C^{-1}$.
method: The analysis employs the AdS/CFT correspondence, calculating transport coefficients via Kubo formulas applied to retarded Green's functions in the near-extremal black brane limit.
model_or_system: The model uses holographic gravity coupled to matter fields (e.g., an isotropic linear axion model) describing a black brane geometry with momentum relaxation mechanisms built into the bulk action.
key_observables: Shear viscosity ($\eta$) and DC electrical conductivity ($\sigma_{DC}$), analyzed through retarded Green's functions.
important_parameters: Low temperature limit ($T 	o 0$), extremal black brane geometry, momentum relaxation scale ($\alpha$), and the Schwarzian scaling dimension ($\Delta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the holographic duality (AdS/CFT) and approximations for quantum corrections in the near-horizon region.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the necessity of quantum corrections due to thermodynamic inconsistencies, then calculating $\eta$ and $\sigma_{DC}$ using advanced techniques involving matched asymptotic expansions and analyzing the order dependence of limits in the Kubo formula application.
why_interesting: The observation of non-monotonic temperature dependence with a minimum, analogous to behavior seen in correlated materials (like strange metals), provides holographic evidence for quantum gravity effects influencing transport in strongly interacting systems.
